newsitem.title: USA: Bear Stearns probed in A.R. Baron case - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Bear Stearns probed in A.R. Baron case - WSJ.

text.p: Trades that Bear Stearns Cos Inc processed for the defunct A.R. Baron & Co are being investigated by federal and New York state authorities, the Wall Street Journal said.

In Monday's electronic edition, the Journal said the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Manhattan District Attorney's office are separately looking into Bear Stearns as part of a wider probe into A.R. Baron.
Last week, a state grand jury indicted A.R. Baron and 13 former employees on accusations they cheated investors out of more than $75 million.
A.R. Baron, which filed for bankruptcy in 1996 and is being liquidated, has denied any wrongdoing.

At issue is what is known as "clearing business," in which small securities firms hire large firms such as Bear Stearns to execute trades, keep client records, send out trade confirmations and monthly statements, and settle transactions.
In particular, the investigation involves how much of a duty clearing firms have to oversee the activities of small securities firms in the transactions it processes.
